item.meaning: The constitutional division of authority among the Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary to prevent power abuse.

item.definition: The organized process of establishing rules, taking collective decisions, and managing public life within a society.
The formal system or institution authorized to formulate, enforce, and interpret laws for a state or nation.
Formal, legally binding rules created by legislative bodies that govern society and maintain public order.
A political system where sovereign power rests with the citizens, exercised directly or through elected representatives.

item.title: Checks and Balances in Governance
item.explanation: The constitutional distribution of authority among Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary prevents any single branch from exercising unchecked power.

item.statement: Satyameva Jayate ('Truth alone triumphs') is India's national motto, taken from the ancient Mundaka Upaniṣhad.
Yato Dharmastato Jayah ('Where there is dharma, there is victory') is the official motto of the Supreme Court of India.

item.name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
item.role_or_contribution: Former President of India and scientist who inspired students with positive interpretations of adversity (e.g. F.A.I.L. = First Attempt In Learning).

item.name: Parliament of India
item.function: The supreme legislative body at the national level responsible for enacting laws, approving budgets, and monitoring the executive.

item.name: Supreme Court of India
item.function: The apex court of India responsible for interpreting the Constitution, upholding fundamental rights, and ensuring executive and legislative compliance.

item.description: The constitutional right granting every adult citizen aged 18 and above the right to vote in democratic elections without discrimination.
The constitutional framework enabling each organ of government (Legislature, Executive, Judiciary) to monitor and limit the power of the other two.

items: 1. Legislature: Body of elected representatives that formulates, amends, or repeals laws.
2. Executive: Administrative branch headed by PM/CM and civil servants that implements laws.
3. Judiciary: Independent court system that interprets laws and delivers justice.

item.category: The Three Levels of Governance in India
items: 1. National / Central Level: Governs the entire country (headquartered in New Delhi).
2. State Level: Governs individual states (e.g. Karnataka, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu).
3. Local Level: Governs local villages (Panchayats) and urban cities (Municipalities).

item.description: Democratic self-governance operating directly at the local community level, enabling citizens to shape decisions directly.
The distinction between a constitutional head of state (President/Governor) and elected political leaders (Prime Minister/Chief Minister).
